speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning. I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; how long has this been present, and have you noticed any changes in its size, color, or drainage?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential, Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR), and C-Reactive Protein (CRP).
REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel (to check for diabetes).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (CBC) - WBC: Within normal limits, Hemoglobin: Within normal limits, Platelets: Within normal limits; Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR): NORMAL READINGS; C-Reactive Protein (CRP): NORMAL READINGS; Basic Metabolic Panel: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, recent injuries, heart disease, or diabetes. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you are denying systemic symptoms and diabetes; to better understand the nature of this wound, has it been associated with any pain, itching, or a specific trigger like insect bites or trauma? Additionally, please confirm if you have any history of varicose veins or previous skin ulcers on this leg.

REQUEST TEST: HbA1c (to definitively rule out diabetes despite initial denial).
REQUEST TEST: Venous Doppler Ultrasound (to assess for venous insufficiency).
REQUEST TEST: Tissue Biopsy (to rule out malignancy or specific infections).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HbA1c: NORMAL READINGS; Venous Doppler Ultrasound: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg; Tissue Biopsy: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the Doppler showing venous reflux and obstruction, combined with the normal biopsy and HbA1c, is the wound located near your ankle with a "red halo" or raised edges? Also, do you experience significant swelling or heaviness in this leg at the end of the day?

REQUEST IMAGES: Color Doppler Ultrasound with spectral analysis of the venous system.
REQUEST TEST: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI).

DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer
